address: Nieuwe Achtergracht 127 (BAG), Amsterdam: UvA Roeterseiland, 1932 brick wing on the Nieuwe Achtergracht / Nieuwe Prinsengracht
notes: Nieuwe Achtergracht 127 (BAG; UvA Roeterseiland), built 1932: a brown-brick teaching wing with a curved NE end. South front on the canal (w03-163, 2021-01-22): four levels (a low ground row of small windows, three storeys of paired windows with red roller shutters, a roof-edge row of small gabled dormers). NE front (w05-30, 2021-01-22): three storeys of wide multi-pane windows in a brick grid under a steep slate roof, a brick chimney and a glazed stair tower at its east end. West end (w01-280, 2020-04-29): a tan rendered rounded block with glass-block panels and a wide curved roof.

Modelled: brick-bay-grid with two-light windows (3.5 cm proud bars) and a cornice on the S and NE fronts (4 storeys, 13 and 12 bays), plain windows on the N and W end walls. Simplified: the low ground row is a full window storey; the red shutters, dormers and the glass stair tower are not drawn. The west block is brick-coloured although the photo shows tan render with glass blocks.

The dark glass-based cantilevered tower on this footprint (twin footprint, pand 0363100012185420, 39 m) is a separate pand and not part of this recipe; panels 62/141 to the west and the east block (w02-253, w06-73) show it.
